items.action: Apply F5's hotfixes immediately and limit exposure of data-plane virtual servers configured as OAuth authorization servers.
items.details: Shadowserver is tracking more than 14,700 exposed instances on the internet. The flaw (CWE-122 heap-based buffer overflow in the OAuth token processing path) is reachable before any authentication check completes, so restricting management-interface access does not protect it.
items.summary: F5 disclosed CVE-2026-94127 on Sept 22, a CVSS 9.8 heap-based buffer overflow that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on BIG-IP APM appliances configured as OAuth authorization servers. F5 confirmed active exploitation before publishing the advisory, and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a Sept 25 patch deadline for federal agencies.
items.title: F5 BIG-IP APM OAuth RCE (CVE-2026-94127) exploited in the wild

items.action: Upgrade SMA 1000 firmware to the fixed releases SonicWall published.
items.details: KEV inclusion confirms real-world exploitation rather than theoretical exposure — an appliance at the network edge landing in the catalog should be treated as a live foothold signal.
items.summary: A CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF in SonicWall SMA 1000 firmware (CVE-2026-83548) moved into CISA's active-exploitation tracker on Sept 23, with observed attacker activity including reverse shells and crypto miners.
items.title: SonicWall SMA 1000 SSRF (CVE-2026-83548) hits CISA's exploited list

items.action: Prioritize these under BOD 26-04 risk-based vulnerability management and verify exposed assets are patched.
items.details: These arrived alongside the F5 BIG-IP APM flaw (CVE-2026-94127) in the same CISA alert batch. KEV inclusion by itself confirms real-world exploitation has occurred.
items.summary: On Sept 22 CISA added CVE-2026-85102 (Check Point improper certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (Check Point path traversal), plus CVE-2026-93952 (Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator improper input validation), to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation.
items.title: CISA adds Check Point and Arista flaws to KEV catalog

items.details: The complaints follow a Sept. 7 claim by the Interlock ransomware group that it compromised NFM Lending and obtained more than 2.5 terabytes of data. That claim has not been independently verified, and NFM Lending had not publicly confirmed the scope in the sources reviewed.
items.summary: At least five lawsuits were filed against NFM Lending LLC in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland between Sept. 11 and Sept. 17 after the mortgage lender was allegedly hit in a ransomware incident that may have exposed sensitive borrower information.
items.title: NFM Lending faces five federal lawsuits after alleged ransomware breach

items.details: OnTrac is a major U.S. parcel-delivery company, so a confirmed compromise could affect customers, merchants, and logistics partners. Neither organization has publicly confirmed the incidents.
items.summary: ThreatMon's feed reports two new ransomware victim claims: OnTrac added by the Emperador group on Sept. 24 and Trump Mobile by the group EndZone on Sept. 23. As with most leak-site listings, the claims should be treated as allegations until corroborated.
items.title: OnTrac and Trump Mobile appear on dark-web ransomware claims

items.action: Treat unsolicited coding tests or video-conferencing "fixes" from recruiters as hostile; never run recruiter-sent code on a work device.
items.details: The agencies said the group poses as recruiters for real AI, crypto, and NFT companies via job boards and freelance marketplaces, then tricks targets into downloading malicious npm packages, repos, or VS Code projects. A compromised developer can become an entry point into an employer's network.
items.summary: A joint Sept. 18 advisory from Japanese, U.S., Australian, and German authorities says North Korea's WaterPlum group (a.k.a. Contagious Interview) infected at least 30,000 devices in over 100 countries between Dec 2025 and July 2026, draining funds or credentials from 7,000+ crypto wallets and moving ~$10.7M to North Korea.
items.title: WaterPlum fake-job campaign infected 30,000 devices, stole $10.7M crypto

items.action: Apply Apple's security updates on iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and Xcode installs now.
items.details: The note covers iOS and iPadOS before 26.7, macOS Golden Gate before 27, macOS Tahoe before 26.7, macOS Sequoia before 15.8, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS before 27, Safari before 27, and Xcode before 27.
items.summary: India's CERT-In published vulnerability note CIVN-2026-0468 on Sept. 21, rating a batch of Apple software flaws high severity. The agency says the flaws could let a remote attacker run arbitrary code, escalate privileges, steal data, or crash devices.
items.title: CERT-In flags high-severity Apple flaws (CIVN-2026-0468), urges updates

items.details: The report does not establish how the attackers gained access, which systems were compromised, whether files were encrypted or data exfiltrated, or whether the university has confirmed the incident.
items.summary: A cybersecurity source reported on Sept. 22 that the AuditTeam ransomware group named VIT in a leak-site claim. Details remain unverified — the report establishes only the claim itself, not the scope of any intrusion.
items.title: AuditTeam claims ransomware attack on VIT; details unverified

items.details: Attacks on energy and utilities providers can disrupt operational workflows beyond ordinary corporate IT, since technology systems are closely tied to service delivery.
items.summary: The Orova ransomware group is linked to an incident against Siddhi Green Excellence Pvt. Ltd. in India, an energy-and-utilities firm, with reports of systems and operations disrupted. Full details of the compromise remain limited in the source reporting.
items.title: Orova ransomware hits Indian energy firm Siddhi Green Excellence
